3. The short facts of the plaintiffs' case are that the suit land measuring 0.4050 acre of land appertaining to BS Khatian 410 and BS Dag Nos. 3253, 3256 and 3276 and an area of 0.36950 acre of land appertaining to BS Khatian No. 411/1 and BS Dag No. 11652 and an area of 0.0790 acre of land appertaining to BS Khatian No. 411/1, total area of 0.16 acre of land under Mouza Cox's Bazar, Upazilla and District-Cox's Bazar originally belonged to Keramat Ali, the predecessor of the plaintiff and the defendants. BS record was duly published in his name. Being the owner and possessor, Keramati Ali left this transitory world leaving behind two sons; plaintiff and defendant No. 1, six daughters i.e. the defendant Nos. 1-5 and the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 6-10. Accordingly, each son obtained 0.0810 acre of land and each daughter obtained 0.0450 acre of land in 'Ka' scheduled property and each son obtained 0.0790 acre of land and each daughter obtained 0.0790 acre of land in 'Kha' scheduled property and they have been possessing their shares by paying rent. The plaintiff in respect of 1(Ka) and 2(Ka) scheduled land got his name mutated in BS Khatian Nos. 6378 and 7042 by mutation case Nos. 2189/2013 and 3417/2017 respectively. The co-sharers are creating obstruction in peaceful possession of the petitioner and are, trying to dispossess the plaintiff from his land; therefore, the plaintiff was constrained to file the aforementioned suit for partition and allocating separate saham in favour of the plaintiff. 

 6. Mr Zulfiqur Ahmed, the learned Advocate along with Ms Rona Naharin Anny appearing for the petitioners submits that admittedly the plaintiff-opposite party and the defendant-petitioners are the children of late Alhaj Keramat Ali who was the original owner of the suit land and after his sad demise, the suit land was amicably partitioned and got their names mutated by Mutation Revision Case No. 6 of 2014 in their respective names and as such, created a new khatian in their respective names. He further submits that in Other Class Suit No. 05 of 2014, both the parties voluntarily compromised and accordingly, they opened separate mutual holdings and paying holding tax separately and having obtained lay out plan from the Cox's Bazar Development Authority, in short 'the CDA' constructed multi-storied building in their respective shares and therefore, there is no jointness of property and as such, it is as clear as day light, the aforesaid suit is hopelessly barred by res judicata and as such, the learned Joint District Judge ought to have rejected the plaint. In support of his contention, he has referred to the decision reported in 27 BLC (AD) 12. He finally submits that if local inspection or local investigation is held, it will be crystal clear that as per the terms of the compromise decree, the parties are in possession of the suit land.
